ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Let n be an integer with n > 1, and let x satisfy (n-1)/n <= x < 1. We prove the two asserted floor identities.

First, fix an integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1. Since x < 1, multiplying by the positive integer k gives kx < k. Also, from x >= (n-1)/n we get

kx >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.

Because k <= n-1 < n, we have k/n < 1, hence k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore

k - 1 <= kx < k.

By the definition of the floor function, the unique integer in the half-open interval [k-1, k) is k-1, so floor(kx) = k - 1.

Now take k = n. From x < 1 we obtain nx < n, and from x >= (n-1)/n we obtain nx >= n-1. Hence

n - 1 <= nx < n.

Again by the definition of the floor function, floor(nx) = n - 1.

Thus for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1 we have floor(kx) = k - 1, and also floor(nx) = n - 1, exactly as claimed.
